NOVELTY STATEMENT — Standard practice delivers a monitoring/indication scheme via online pH feedback; this proposal delivers a DESIGN CHANGE (procedure modification) by decoupling dosing from the drift-prone sensor and anchoring the dosing setpoint to the already-recorded weekly lab titration data, using the caustic dosing pump stroke rate as the sole permitted control variable to maintain inlet pH below 10.5.
PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is carbonate scale precipitation rate proportional to $(pH - pH_{sat})^n$; driving variable = inlet pH; the mechanism moves it DOWN by reducing average caustic dose via a fixed 70% stroke rate derived from titration deficit, thereby lowering the scale precipitation integral over the duty cycle.
IMPLEMENTATION BILL — MECHANISM CLASS: Open-loop titration-anchored stroke-rate modulation.
(a) Dosing-pump stroke rate setpoint register: **ALREADY-RECORDED** (DCS setpoint register).
(b) Weekly lab titration results: **ALREADY-RECORDED** (stated problem text).
(c) Caustic dosing pump stroke rate: **DERIVED** (Calculation: 70% of current stroke rate, derived from titration deficit to maintain pH < 10.5).
BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — Installability: None (existing DCS). Operability: Low (weekly titration review, manual setpoint update). Maintenance: Zero (no new probes). Cost: Zero hardware, <1% operational availability loss due to reduced caustic inventory turnover; trade nets positive by avoiding membrane replacement costs (orders of magnitude higher than titration labor).
EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Execute 70% stroke rate for 4 weeks against weekly titration; instruments: Lab titration kit, DCS log; pass/fail: Inlet pH < 10.5 in DCS log, no titration deficit >5%; duration: 4 weeks; kill criterion: pH > 10.5 for two consecutive daily readings or titration deficit >10%.
CONSTRAINT BIND (predictor) — The primary stated indicator is caustic dosing pump stroke rate (the ONLY permitted control variable); weekly lab titration is the DERIVED reference that anchors the setpoint, not a control input; pH is monitored but explicitly excluded from the control loop per constraint.
